reviews.review_text:
I lived at Galleria Palms for 2 years.  Sure, the place is full of potheads, but what do you expect from a place that hosts a bunch of ASU students?  (No offense to those who actually go to ASU to get a degree).

The main pool is phenomenal; I miss that pool the most!  The fitness center is great and none of the machinery snags like at the current place I live.  The office people are generally nice but most of the time they're unsure of policies.  They have some dumb rules, like giving you a pass which you must present to the security guards should you ever get questioned.

And about security--they only ask people to prove they live in the apartment complex at night.  All they ask for though is what apartment you live in, so basically you could just make up a random number and they'd accept that.  It's kinda crappy security.

The reason I stated it is best to live here if you don't have a car is because during my stay at Galleria, two of my roommates got their cars broken into.  One of my roommates got her tire stolen with her own tire jack!!  The other got her CD player stolen.  However, the first roommate had had the car sitting there for 5  months because it died in October and she didn't bother even TRYING to get it fixed until June, when the tire jacking happened.  The other roommate was a complete idiot and left her car door unlocked.  Both of these girls also didn't have alarms on their car.

Another reason it is good to live here if you DON'T have a car is because the parking SUCKS!!  You only get one parking spot assigned to you and half of the time that's taken by a stupid visitor (however, they do tow cars at Galleria like nobody's business.)  On a Friday night, you have to get home early if you want a parking spot anywhere!  


The walls at Galleria are also paper thin, but I'm beginning to think that all apartment complex in the Phoenix area are like that.  You can hear people coming and going, the air conditioner on the bottom floor vibrates the top floor, and if you live next to party hosts, expect to be kept up late at night (unless you're one of those people who call the police for noise complaints.)

So if you can deal with car theft, annoying security, and loud noises, Galleria shouldn't be too bad of a place for you.

My fiance and I own three cars.  We have been in the process of trying to sell two of them.  I have let registration lapse on one of them.  The same car has a flat tire. Since the car was there, with a flat, for a bit of time and not moved - the manager decided to tow the vehicle with their partners ACT Towing - which they have a nice agreement with in towing any vehicles out of their parking lot.  

Now - here is what happened - we were given a warning about the vehicle and not being registered and how it may get towed about two months ago. I had already checked with MVD, and they confirmed that as long as it is not being driven, and insured - I can take as long as I need to sell it, with no penalties.

I explained this to someone at the management office, who apparently does not work there anymore.  Not my problem.  Since I have been here for over two years, it is the business of the management complex to keep track of these kinds of warnings, and how their tenants tried to resolve it.  

We received another notice 4 days ago, then one 2 days ago - absolutely did not have time to stop in the office - I have a full time job and also run a real estate investment company and upon arriving back to the apartment, car was gone.  

Called the office - was told it was towed.  Manager authorized it and cited it was on my lease.  I explained situation again - and she said there was nothing she could do about it.  Just call ACT Towing and get my car back - and threatened to have the vehicle towed if the vehicle came back unregistered.  Since when did the management at Galleria Palms become DOT?  Apparently the management company does not care to handle each and every case as a unique one, and they use the blanket policy to cover themselves.  Give me a break, my car was not on cinder blocks with plastic on the windows or on a jack for weeks at a time.  I have seen all of that in the parking lot within the last two years.  

I do not want to see broken down and junk cars in my parking lot.  The vehicle we own is far from that, and just had a flat tire - and was not moved.  Driving out of the apartment complex this morning, we had noted several vehicles that are in desperate need of towing if our vehicle qualified for it.  

My fiance had rented at Galleria Palms when it first opened, and suggested it when we were in transition because she had an "OK" experience there.  NEVER AGAIN.  The quality of tenants moving into the complex has dropped, as I can see who lives around me.  The college crowd has not changed since we moved in - and that does not bother us. Besides, rents have been steadily increasing, and this place is not worth it.  There are bug problems here as well, and I have had to call management on several occasions.  We are clean people and do not leave food everywhere.  

Do not let the pretty little fountains spouting joy and happiness in the front of the complex fool and seduce you.  You will quickly come to the realization that it is a sham to get your hard-earned cash.

I don't have exact estimates with me, but I can say that I have probably spent upwards of 18 THOUSAND DOLLARS IN RENT here.  Do they care about that kind of customer?  The answer is a BIG FAT NO.

We have lived here for 2 1/2 years, and are moving out because we want more of a luxurious place to live in a better location. Galleria Palms has been nice for the stay we had here. 

I have a few issues for people to be aware of before they move in. Firstly, the front gate rarely works - so do not move here for the safety of a gated community, it might as well not be. My boyfriend's car was broken into as well (and we live right near the front desk), so make sure to at least put a club on your steering wheel at night. 

Second, main pool is often closed because people bring glass in to the pool area. If maintenance or any staff found any glass, the pool would be closed the next day. This was frustrating because the pool is very fun and beautiful to hang out at, so to arrive there to find it closed is discouraging. They do keep the other pools open when this happens, but it is still frustrating. 

Third, there can be a lot of little kids running around at times. They were never very annoying, but I personally don't like to hang out with kids when I am drinking with friends at the pool. I'm sure families thought us drinking at the pool was annoying too though, so I guess it goes both ways. 

Overall, it has been a good experience. We are not moving for any bad reason; just want a change of scenery. The office staff and maintenance are very friendly and reliable. I would say the majority of people living here are college kids, so take that into account if that is not what you are looking for. We lived on the second floor and had no problems with noise. I really think a lot of people post on here because they feel very strongly against or for a place. That being said, I found no serious problems here and I recommend giving it a try. Anywhere you live there will be good and bad.

reviews.review_text:
For Tempe this place is really good.  I'm actually only moving because ADOT is buying the buildings running along the 10/60 for highway expansion and I don't have a choice about that but I knew this might happen when I signed the lease.

I'm having a really hard time finding something as good in the same price range in Tempe and the plethora of nasty reviews for just about every place I look at on here prompted me to look up this place.  Puts my concerns into perspective.  

Tip from a fellow apartment dweller is always screen the unit before signing the lease and again before leaving and get everything in writing and signed as necessary.  It seems a lot of people haven't read or don't understand the landlord/tenant act.  Google it.  Both landlords and tenants have certain rights but by signing the lease you are legally agreeing to follow it's provisions, I'd suggest reading them first.  You wouldn't sign to buy/finance a car without looking at the price, interest rate, and terms would you?

Pros:

Good size apartment floor plans (more space than i need)
Full sized washer/dryer in unit (1 load of laundry once a week in my case)
Maintenance (my thermostat and heater broke they replaced both within 48 hours even though my unit was scheduled to be torn down, emergency maintenance responded quickly as well ... see cons for that night of fun)
Plenty of extra open parking compared to other places (easy to invite friends or have multiple vehicles)
Good amenities overall (small gym, but indoor basketball court makes up for that)

reviews.review_text:
These apartments are liars, thieves, and scandals. Don't trust them. I have never been so disappointed in any place I have lived as I was with Galleria Palms apartments. 

When I first moved in I was excited to be getting such a great deal on such nice apartments. Within a week of moving in several residents approached my brother and I telling us they felt bad for us having just moved in since everyone in our building would have to move out soon. Funny how it was never mentioned to us that we might have to move not long after moving in. The only thing ever mentioned to us was on the day we were signing our lease they mentioned ADOT had taken over some of their buildings due to construction that was going on nearby. They said it wasn't anything to worry about though. About 2 months later we were notified that we either had to find another apartment within 30 days or move into the apartment they offered us. Since we had just paid move in costs to move into the apartment we ended up taking the apartment they offered since that option meant we didn't have to pay security costs again. When we went to move into the apartment they offered they insisted we had to sign another year lease instead of just continuing the lease we had previously. They only allowed us one week to move from one apartment to the other even though nobody was moving into the previous apartment any time soon and we would have had more time if we just moved some where else.

Fast forward 3 or 4 months later. My brother and I went on vacation thinking the nightmare was done. When we came home a week later our parking area was fenced off and we had no place to park. We went in to find out why we didn't have a parking spot and why we weren't given any notice about this situation either. The lady in the office was rude and kept telling us we still had the same parking number. She said they put a note on our door as soon as they knew about it. Granted I will admit my brother and I were both beyond upset after the first incident and then this. Yet I still believe customer service requires that a person try to disarm the situation instead of making it worse. I have worked customer service my whole life and I would never have approached an upset customer the way she approached us.

Now move forward to months later when the construction is over. We received a paper (on our door again)stating our parking number may change, but our space should remain the same. We ended up finding out from a new tenant that our parking space changed. This happened when my brother was about to have the person's car towed, but found out who the person was and talked to them. Again Galleria Palms did not communicate information to us and when confronted flat out lied about having communicated the change to us.

Due to all these problems my brother and I decided to speed up our plans on finding a house. Now come to present day. My brother kept checking Galleria Palms website for a bill to see how much we owed if any. Day after day there was no bill that appeared. As is Galleria Palms way we finally got a bill from them. The kicker on this is they are charging us for a spot on the carpet that neither my brother nor I know about (and I went over all spots with my steam cleaner)and they want the full amount of $878.70 within 7 days. 

The problems with this is: First by tenant laws and all payment laws they have to allow a reasonable amount of time from the time the person being charged receives the bill to pay the bill. Seven days is not a reasonable amount of time by law and in reality. Second they only sent the bill out as of 1/4/2013. So where they get the idea that they legally have the right to set a payment due date of 1/14/2013 is beyond me. Third after all the above issues we have I really feel that they should pay my brother and I for having to deal with them. 

My advice go live in the roach invested Midtown on Main before moving into Galleria Palms. At least then you will receive communication and honesty on what is going on. I would rather have roaches since I can get roach spray and roach motels to kill them than deal with an apartment complex who lies to me and does dishonest business.
